tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Social Stratification & Class

questions.question: Explain what social stratification is and how social class affects life chances.
questions.correctAnswer: Stratification divides society into layers based on wealth, power and status. Class dramatically affects life chances: health, education, income, housing. These inequalities persist across generations.

questions.question: Describe the extent of wealth inequality in the UK and evaluate explanations for it.
questions.correctAnswer: Top 10% own 44% of wealth; bottom 50% own 9%. Marxist: capitalism concentrates wealth. Wilkinson and Pickett: inequality harms everyone. Some inequality may incentivise effort, but extreme inequality is harmful.

questions.question: Evaluate whether social class is still relevant in modern society.
questions.correctAnswer: Class still affects health, education, income, housing. Counter: class identities are weakening; social mobility exists. Conclusion: class is less culturally significant but its material impact remains powerful.
